title: RunFlux pocket slate — weekly microflow scorecard
content:
Purpose:
Small personal ledger for quick turnaround microbench experiments around RunFlux batching/config variants. Use this to capture a single-week snapshot (quick numbers + top takeaways) so I don’t lose the little heuristics I keep re-running.

Legend / columns (single-line):
- id | date | config-note | prompt-dist (avg tok) | batch | concurrent | req/s observed | p50 ms | p95 ms | avg tokens | cost/1k toks est | notes

Rows (most recent on top):
R-2026-02-18 | 2026-02-18 | baseline-quant-4bit | 48 | 8 | 16 | 420 | 48 | 230 | 56 | $0.22 | Good steady req/s. KV warm hit ~78%
R-2026-02-15 | 2026-02-15 | batch=16 prefactor | 48 | 16 | 12 | 540 | 62 | 290 | 55 | $0.18 | latency pushed slightly; tails worse for long prompts
R-2026-02-12 | 2026-02-12 | kv-ttl-120s | 120 | 8 | 8 | 360 | 72 | 330 | 118 | $0.14 | KV helps for repeat prefix; cost drops but cold starts costly
R-2026-02-09 | 2026-02-09 | small-prompt-sample | 12 | 4 | 24 | 310 | 28 | 110 | 14 | $0.30 | tiny prompts favor low batch; throughput limited by per-request overhead
R-2025-11-21 | 2025-11-21 | quant-8bit + cache | 64 | 12 | 10 | 470 | 54 | 210 | 65 | $0.20 | Stable; quant artifacts low for this workload

Quick calcs (back-of-envelope):
- Cost per successful 1k tokens = (tokens_per_req * req/s * runtime_seconds) scaled -> used local price $0.00022/tokenk in notes above (est).
- When concurrency > 16 for batch sizes 8-16 we see p95 climb rapidly (observed flip point around concurrency 18-20 for this model/hardware).

Open hypotheses / TODOs:
- Hyp1: reducing KV TTL from 120s -> 60s increases cache churn but reduces memory footprint; measure p50/p95 for mixed prompt set. (next run R-2026-03-x)
- Hyp2: dynamic batch sizing based on prompt length binning should give ~8–12% cost win without hurting p95; need to write short script to simulate mix.
- TODO: push sample scripts into runflux repo (GH: repo/runflux#432) and attach a small CSV import into this sheet for automatic row add.

Notes to self / shorthand: 
- "warm hit" = KV present + same prefix → big latency win. Track hit% daily.
- For short prompts (<=32 tokens) prefer batch <=4 and concurrency >=16; for med prompts (32–128) batch 8–12.
- Keep one weekly snapshot with full raw traces (p50/p90/p95/p99) saved into GH artifact storage.

Scratch calculations (today):
- If avg tokens per req = 56 and we do 500 req/s for 60s: total tokens = 56*500*60 = 1,680,000 tokens -> ~1680k -> cost at $0.22/1k = $0.3696 -> ~$0.37 for that minute.
- If batching takes us to 700 req/s but avg tokens increases to 65: tokens = 65*700*60 = 2,730,000 -> 2730k -> cost $0.6006 -> tradeoff: throughput vs unit cost.

Last-minute learnings (summary):
- KV caching is high leverage for conversational reuse but fragile across prompt mutations; need better similarity thresholds for re-use.
- Batch tuning per-prompt-length bin seems promising; next week run targeted bins + dynamic batching simulation.

Slack crumbs & refs:
- Slack thread: #runflux-bench (search: "kv-ttl anom 2026-02-12")
- Confluence note (draft): CON-RunFlux-batching-v1 (will link when tidy)

End of pocket slate.
